description: Sabotages for windows-file-enumeration-sys. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are. Begun with PATH-1, so it covers the path contract this crate now takes from windows-namespace-request-sys and nothing older.
notCoveredHere: The graft's own rules are the request crate's and are sabotaged in its manifest (the NR-3.3 entries); this one covers only this crate's use of them. A failure to read the current directory cannot be made by a test, so the code it carries is a declared survivor.

sabotages.name: SAFE-1: the identity is read from a different file than the one enumerated
sabotages.why: The test now hands the request crate a SharedHandle made from the opened file; this shows the comparison still tells one file from another rather than passing on any identity.

sabotages.name: SAFE-1 control: the same file is opened another way
sabotages.why: A control: how the file is opened is incidental; which file it is, is what the test claims.

sabotages.name: PATH-1: the worker opens the path as given and not the grafted one
sabotages.why: The two name the same directory until the current directory moves, so only the child-process test that moves it after the request is built tells them apart. Since SAFE-2 the open takes the request's AnchoredPath, so this opens the given path anchored again at open time instead.

sabotages.name: PATH-1: the path as given is reported as the grafted one
sabotages.why: path() is documented as the path the caller gave, and a relative one differs from what the worker opens.

sabotages.name: PATH-1: an interior NUL is reported as a failure to read the current directory
sabotages.why: The two failures say different things to the caller, and only the first is about the path itself.

sabotages.name: PATH-1: the code of a failure to read the current directory is dropped
sabotages.why: Declared, and not a gap a test can close: GetCurrentDirectoryW cannot be made to fail from a test without breaking the process it runs in. What would reach it is a fault seam in the request crate's current-directory read, which it does not have.

sabotages.name: PATH-1 control: the request's path is built through a binding
sabotages.why: A control: the same value through a local, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
replace:
Ok(Self {
            path: { let anchored = path; anchored },

sabotages.name: SAFE-2: the open drops delete sharing
sabotages.why: A held enumeration would stop a rename of its directory; the rename test and the request-shape test see it.

sabotages.name: SAFE-2: the open asks for read access instead of listing
sabotages.why: M21.3's constraint: listing access and not GENERIC_READ, so a directory a caller may list but not read still opens.

sabotages.name: SAFE-2: the open drops backup semantics
sabotages.why: Without it CreateFileW fails on any directory.

sabotages.name: SAFE-2: the open adds the overlapped flag
sabotages.why: The handle must not be overlapped; the request-shape test pins the flags to backup semantics alone.

sabotages.name: SAFE-2: the first refill continues instead of restarting
sabotages.why: The first query restarts the enumeration; the class test sees the swap.

sabotages.name: SAFE-2: every directory is taken for one
sabotages.why: FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY opens an ordinary file too; the check is what keeps naming a file from reading as a capability failure.

sabotages.name: SAFE-2: the volume serial is reported as zero
sabotages.why: A real volume's serial is non-zero.

sabotages.name: SAFE-2: a refused refill buffer is reported as exhaustion
sabotages.why: Declared: the arm cannot be reached. The request crate refuses a buffer ahead of the call only for classes whose structure page requires an alignment, neither extended-directory class is one, and this buffer is 8-aligned besides. What would reach it is a refusal added to those classes' table.

sabotages.name: SAFE-2 control: the volume serial is read through a binding
sabotages.why: A control: the same value through a local, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: SAFE-3: the shared wait target is a second event, not the ring's
sabotages.why: A wait armed on a separate event would never be woken by the ring; the shared-handle test and the thread pool test see it.

sabotages.name: SAFE-3: the doorbell is set when nothing is pending and reset when something is
sabotages.why: The doorbell's one invariant, inverted.

sabotages.name: SAFE-3: the doorbell starts unsignalled however much has already arrived
sabotages.why: A client that asks for the doorbell after records have arrived must find it signalled.

sabotages.name: SAFE-3: the doorbell is never refreshed
sabotages.why: Without the refresh the event stays as it was created.
replace:
let _ = event;
        let refreshed: io::Result<()> = Ok(());

sabotages.name: SAFE-3 control: the shared target is made through a binding
sabotages.why: A control: the same clone through a local, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
